**ID**: `cpt-{system}-literature-{slug}`

## Table of Contents

## 1. Request

- PLAN: `cpt-{system}-plan-{slug}`
- Literature mode: {`allowed` | `blind`, copied from the PLAN's section 2. A PLAN whose mode is `none` produces no LITERATURE.}
- Exclusions checked: {under `blind`, the number of rows of the PLAN's Excluded table; the gate fails if it differs from the PLAN's row count. `not applicable` under `allowed`.}
- Strategy: {`related` | `review` | `metareview` | `scout`}
- Anchor: {DOI or OpenAlex id (a title, arXiv id or draft is resolved to a DOI at intake); or Subject: the subject with its must-have terms}
- Bounds: {only the bounds applied on this run, as `lit_run.py` writes them: `since <year>` for `review` run with `--since`, otherwise `no year bound`; for `scout` followed by `; quantity <quantity> [<unit>]`}
- Depth: {`quick` | `deep` for `review`; `-n <N>`, the cap on the total Set, for the other strategies}
- Output shape: {…}
- Cost stated before running: {written by the agent before the run: OpenAlex credits estimated as search 10, work 1, group_by 10, title search 10, online gate 1 per DOI; Consensus calls}
- Cost used: {retrieval credits and requests as written by `lit_run.py`; the agent adds the online gate's DOI lookups and the total against the stated cost}

## 2. Sources

{One row per source. The `ran` cell is `yes`, `no`, `skipped (<reason>)` or `not configured`. A `yes` row records the canonical query so a person can rerun it. Nothing substituted silently.}

| source | ran | query or tool calls | budget used | note |
|--------|-----|---------------------|-------------|------|
| OpenAlex | yes / no / skipped (reason) | {canonical query URL} | {credits} | {…} |
| Consensus | yes / no / skipped (reason) / not configured | {query, filters, page_size} | {calls} | {plan} |
| Hypothesis | yes / no / skipped (reason) / not configured | {collection id, tools} | — | {coverage, see section 4} |

- Removed by exclusion: {under `blind`, the number of retrieved papers removed from the Set because they matched an item of the PLAN's Excluded table: the count only, never the matched DOI, title, term, benchmark or author; `not applicable` under `allowed`.}

## 3. Set

{Every paper the analysis may cite, one line each. `#`: the row's number, a unique positive integer; numbers need not be contiguous, and trimming the Set deletes rows without renumbering the rest. Role, as `lit_run.py` writes it: Path 1 `reference` / `citer` / `related` / `same-topic`; Path 2 `anchor` / `snowball` / `set`; Path 3 `review`; Path 4 `candidate (N signals)`. Resolved: `yes` | `unresolved` | `no DOI`; `yes` when the DOI returned a record from OpenAlex on this run, `no DOI` with the DOI cell `—`. Approved by: the person who approved the set and the date (P12). A paper not in this table is not cited anywhere below. Under `blind` no row matches an excluded item.}

| # | DOI | year | title | role | cited by | resolved | OA link |
|---|-----|------|-------|------|----------|----------|---------|

- Approved by: {person, YYYY-MM-DD}

## 4. Collection

{Only when Hypothesis ran. Collection id and name; coverage as `k of N`: papers of the approved set indexed in the collection over papers in the approved set, N equal to the number of Set rows and k ≤ N; the DOIs the collection lacks; index date. A claims map built on a collection that holds less than half the approved set is a map of the uploads, not of the subject: a `draft` may record such coverage, and the gate refuses `verified` on it. Write `not used` otherwise.}

## 5. Analysis

{Path 1: the prior work grouped by sub-problem — what was established, by whom, with which method, and what the anchor adds. Path 2: one block per group (authors, institutions, approach, data, years active, achievements in the Set's own terms, assessment: succeeding / stalled / too early, with evidence), then the cross-group observations. Path 3: per review its scope, period, trends and gaps; then trends asserted by several reviews, trends contradicted between reviews, what no review covers; no primary-source claims. Path 4: the scout table `set # | paper | doi | link | what_measured | how_measured | constraints | value | unit | passage`, one row per measurement, with constraints in the paper's words and units copied, never converted; the same rows, as many and in the same order, are written as CSV beside this artifact (column `set_no` for `set #`). A value cell is filled only with its passage. Its values are claims, not data: they reach a PLAN only through section 6 and never become a DATASET.

Every sentence of prose that asserts something about a paper ends with its Set row number in brackets, e.g. `[3]` or `[3, 5-7]`; the Analysis cites at least one Set row. The request's anchor is named without a row number; every other paper is cited by Set row. Citations are read only from prose outside tables and code; in a table of this section a paper is cited by its `set #` cell, and the other cells (passages and quotes, verbatim) are not read as citations. A paper not in the Set may not be mentioned.}

## 6. Claims

{Each claim the PLAN may use. Claims row n is the n-th data row of the Claims table, counted from 1 in table order; rows are never reordered or deleted after a PLAN cites them. Citations read `<LITERATURE ID>, claim n`. Quote: the paper's words; for a scout value, the passage it came from. Location: section and paragraph, or page, where the quote was found on this run. The claim cell says no more than the quote shows. Status: `verified` when the row's Set `resolved` cell is `yes` and the quote was located; `assumed` otherwise. A verified claim may license a parameter range or a mechanism in the PLAN; an assumed claim is handed over as `assumed` and may motivate a diagnostic batch only, never a parameter range or a mechanism (P10). A row enters the PLAN's section 2 only after a person approves it (P12).}

| claim | set # | quote | location | status |
|-------|-------|-------|----------|--------|

## 7. Candidate Hypotheses

{Where the Set contradicts itself — two groups, two reviews, two measurements that disagree — one candidate per contradiction, as a proposed row for the PLAN's Hypothesis Space: mechanism or effect, the claims it rests on (cited as `claim n`, rows of section 6), a proposed diagnostic condition, status NOT YET TESTED. A candidate whose cited claims are all `assumed` is marked `assumed only` in its candidate cell: it may motivate a diagnostic batch, and it is not proposed for the PLAN's section 8 as a mechanism. Proposed, never confirmed: the human confirms it in the PLAN. Write `none` if the Set is consistent.}

| candidate | claims | proposed diagnostic condition | status |
|-----------|--------|-------------------------------|--------|

## 8. Attestation

{One bullet per line, in these forms. The gate reads only the `Set approved by` line (L2, when the status is `verified`) and the `Gate, online:` lines (L9); the other lines are for the record.
- Retrieval: `<lit_run invocation>`, run <YYYY-MM-DD>; {lit_run.py version, sources and endpoints, requests, cost}
- Literature mode confirmed by <person>, <YYYY-MM-DD> (<PLAN section 11 | conversation>); under `blind` the line ends `; Excluded table confirmed`.
- Set approved by <person>, <YYYY-MM-DD>.
- Hand-over to `<PLAN ID>` section 2: {claims n, …, each `verified` or `assumed`}; approved by <person>, <YYYY-MM-DD>.
- Gate, offline|online: `<invocation exactly as run>`, run <YYYY-MM-DD>: PASS|FAIL; {DOIs looked up, credits, notes}
One gate line per invocation. The label `online` requires `--resolve` and `--plan` in the invocation; any other invocation is `offline`. Status `verified` needs an `online` PASS (L9). An edit made after a gate run is recorded in one line saying what changed, followed by the line of the gate rerun.}
